title: Streptomycin (historical)
dek: The 1940s aminoglycoside that launched combination therapy. rpsL K43/K88, rrs 514 region, gid. Ototoxicity, pregnancy ban, not a 2025 preferred drug.
story: Streptomycin was the first really effective TB antibacterial and the reason combination therapy had to be invented (resistance emerged on monotherapy in months). It binds the 30S subunit. Clinical resistance: rpsL K43R/K88R, rrs mutations in the 514/517 neighbourhood, gidB loss-of-function (a 16S methyltransferase-adjacent story).

It is not AMK. rpsL K43R does not automatically clear or condemn amikacin. WHO does not want STR in preferred 6-month orals. Some older national DS overlays still mention S as a fifth drug in meningitis or when EMB cannot be used — check the year of the SOP.
Pregnancy: no. Audiometry: yes if you still inject it. PubChem CID 19649.
deepTitle: Why labs still must decode it
deep: Archive genomes and retreatment patients carry rpsL alleles. They explain old failures; they do not define 2021-XDR.
Do not call AMK-R from rpsL alone.
gid frameshifts can be lineage-associated in some studies — grade them.
Historical monotherapy papers are how you teach mutation supply, not how you treat today.

example.title: rpsL K43R flagged as “injectable R”
example.setup: A junior report lists AMK-R because rpsL K43R is present. rrs 1401 WT, eis WT.

steps.title: Wrong injectable
steps.body: K43R is a streptomycin allele. AMK is a 1401/eis question.

steps.title: STR is still not a good idea
steps.body: Genetically dead STR, and you probably did not want STR anyway.

steps.title: If salvage injectable is truly needed, MIC AMK
steps.body: Do not skip MIC because a different aminoglycoside gene fired.
